Regulation: B.C. Reg. 146/2026
Made under: Post - Secondary International Education (Designated Institutions) Act
Published in: No. 14 – B.C. Regs. 125 to 148, July 28, 2026
Deposit date: July 24, 2026

B.C. Reg. 146/2026, deposited July 24, 2026, under thePOST-SECONDARY INTERNATIONAL EDUCATION (DESIGNATED INSTITUTIONS) ACT[sections 2, 3, 4 (2), 7 (1), 9, 33 (2) and (3) and 38]. Order in Council 363/2026, approved and ordered July 24, 2026. On the recommendation of the undersigned, the Lieutenant Governor, by and with the advice and consent of the Executive Council, orders that (a)	effective September 1, 2026, thePost-Secondary International Education (Designated Institutions) Act, S.B.C. 2026, c. 4, except sections 4 (2) (c), 12, 21 (2) (b) and 36 (3), is brought into force, (b)	effective September 1, 2026, the attached Post-Secondary International Education (Designated Institutions) Regulation is made and comes into force as follows: (i)	Part 1 is brought into force on September 1, 2026; (ii)	Part 2 is brought into force on January 1, 2027, and (c)	effective January 1, 2027, sections 4 (2) (c), 12, 21 (2) (b) and 36 (3) of thePost-Secondary International Education (Designated Institutions) Actare brought into force. — J. SUNNER,Minister of Post-Secondary Education and Future Skills; N. SHARMA,Presiding Member of the Executive Council. POST-SECONDARY INTERNATIONAL EDUCATION(DESIGNATED INSTITUTIONS) REGULATION "Act"means thePost-Secondary International Education (Designated Institutions) Act; "National Occupational Classification"means the National Occupational Classification developed by Employment and Social Development Canada and Statistics Canada and their successors, as amended from time to time; "theological institution"means an institution that offers either of the following: (a)	a diploma or certificate relating to an occupation described in the current edition of the National Occupational Classification as follows: Advertising prohibition – minimum duration of program of instruction 2For the purposes of section 2 (a) of the Act, an institution must not advertise a program of instruction of a duration that exceeds 6 months. 3For the purposes of section 3 (a) (iv) of the Act, the following institutions are prescribed: (a)	an institution that is a theological institution; (b)	an institution that offers educational programs referred to in section 31 (1) of theChartered Professional Accountants Act; (c)	an institution that offers training for an occupation of driving motor vehicles that requires a driver to hold a Class 1, 2 or 3 driver’s licence under theMotor Vehicle Act; (d)	Lester B. Pearson College of the Pacific and United World Colleges (Canada) Inc.

minutes_briefs.title: BC's new international education law starts September 1, 2026, with more rules coming January 1, 2027
minutes_briefs.summary: BC has brought into force the Post-Secondary International Education (Designated Institutions) Act, a law that governs schools that enrol international students. Most of the Act and Part 1 of its regulation start on September 1, 2026. Part 2 of the regulation and a few remaining sections of the Act start on January 1, 2027. The regulation also sets rules, including a ban on advertising programs longer than 6 months and a list of institutions that are exempt from certain requirements.
minutes_briefs.action_required: Check whether your school is covered by the Act and update your advertising and enrolment practices before September 1, 2026.

key_dates.label: BC international education Act and Regulation Part 1 take effect
BC international education Regulation Part 2 takes effect
Remaining BC international education Act sections take effect
